subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.

spec.name: Warhound 77 Armored Truck
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk militarized 6x6 truck from 2077 with armored cab, roof turret railgun, neon underglow and a modular cargo bed.
spec.layout: A heavy 6x6 armored truck facing +Z. Front to back: a sloped armored bumper with winch and plow blade (z 3.5..4.0), a low angular hood with vents and a glowing grille, a tall wedge cab (z 0.9..2.9) with narrow slit windshield and side armor skirts, a roof turret ring at the cab/cargo seam, then a long boxy cargo bed (z -3.8..0.8) with ribbed armor, missile pods and a rear ramp. Three axles of big chunky tyres with hex hubcaps sit at z=2.6, -0.6, -2.9, wheel centres y=0.62, tyre radius 0.62. Hull is dark gunmetal with hazard-yellow trim stripes, cyan and magenta neon strips along the skirts, headlights and underglow; panelled/riveted paints and SVG decals (unit number 77, hazard chevrons, kanji-like glyphs, warning labels) carry the intricate detail. All shapes are chunky faceted primitives with low segment counts.

parts.builds: Ladder frame and underbody: two long box rails with cross-members, drive shafts, differentials at each axle, exhaust stacks, fuel tanks, suspension leaf springs and shock absorbers at the three axles, mudguard arches over each wheel, a panelled-iron belly skid plate with rivets, side skirt armor panels with neon cyan strips along the lower edge and magenta underglow bars, hazard-chevron SVG decal strips on the skirts. All parts ride body.
parts.attaches: Top at frameTop supports cabFloor and bedFloor; axle lines at axleFront/axleMid/axleRear carry the wheel joints.

parts.builds: Six chunky low-poly tyres (octagonal-faceted cylinders radius 0.62, width 0.55) with deep tread-block ring details, steel hex hubcaps with bolt rings, glowing cyan hub accent discs, brake discs and calipers visible behind, mud paint at the bottom. Each wheel rides its own wheel joint, centred at x=±1.3 on the axle lines; tyre bottoms touch y=0.

Armored wedge cab body from cabFloor to cabRoof (z 0.9..2.9): faceted lofted shell with sloped windshield frame, narrow slit glass windows (glass colour with SVG reflection streak texture), side armor plates with bolts, door outlines with handles, side mirrors as camera pods, roof hatch, antenna array and sensor dome, roof rack rails, roof emergency light bars (red/cyan glowing), interior glimpse (seats, dashboard with glowing screens) behind glass, panelled hull paint, big '77' and unit glyph decals on the doors.
parts.attaches: Sits on cabFloor; front meets cabFront at z=2.9; rear meets cargo at z=0.9; roof at cabRoof.

parts.builds: Front end z 2.9..4.0: sloped hood with vents and ribs, glowing neon grille with SVG mesh/skull emblem texture, angular headlight clusters (lampWhite glowing, with cyan DRL strips), armored bumper with yellow hazard stripes, winch drum with cable and hook, plow/ram blade with teeth, tow hooks, front fender flares over the front wheels, fog lamps, antenna whip, radar plates, spike studs along the bumper, glowing magenta underglow.
parts.attaches: Meets cabShell at z=2.9, chassis frame at the bottom, hoodFront mount.

parts.builds: Roof-mounted remote weapon station on turretRing: lathe ring base with gear teeth, rotating faceted armored housing with sloped plates, sensor eye cluster with glowing red lens (SVG), shoulder ammo box with belt feed, twin ammo drums, vents, antenna, yellow trim, and a long railgun: twin parallel rails barrel with coil rings glowing cyan, muzzle brake, heat fins, on gunPitch joint. Housing rides turretYaw, gun rides gunPitch (barrel muzzle reaches z=2.9 at y~3.0).
parts.attaches: Base at turretRing (0,2.62,0.55) on roof/bed seam; joints turretYaw, gunPitch.

parts.builds: Armored modular cargo box from bedFloor to z -3.8..0.9: ribbed side walls with paneled riveted paint, top deck with hatches, fold-down rear ramp on rampHinge with hazard stripes, side-mounted missile pod racks (angled tubes with warheads), stacked crates and ammo cans on the deck, antenna, tie-down rings, tail lights (red glow), license plate decal, spare tyre mount, rear neon magenta strip, vent stacks and an exhaust pair, cyan glowing status panels and SVG warning labels.
parts.attaches: Sits on bedFloor/frameTop; front wall meets cabShell at z=0.9; ramp hinge at rearDeck; turretRing at z=0.55 y=2.62 sits on its front top.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working on the turret-building function, setting up the context parameters and planning the yaw joint positioning.

Now I'm laying out the physical structure: placing the base ring, housing box, gun rails, and coil rings while keeping everything within the bounding box limits. I'm figuring out torus orientation for the coil rings and sketching the housing's sloped profile using extruded geometry defined in z-y coordinates.

I'm adding side cheek plates with trim stripes, positioning an olive ammo box on one flank, and planning twin ammo drums near the back of the turret.

For the belt feed, I'm sweeping a curved path from the ammo box toward the gun breech, routing it through a few control points to create a smooth, mechanically plausible connection in matching ammo-colored material.

Now I'm designing the sensor eye cluster on the front housing: a black cylindrical eye socket with a glowing red lens decal plane, sloped to the housing's angle, arranged as a cluster with one larger central eye and smaller flanking ones.

Adding vents, antenna, and gear teeth...

Adding trim boxes on the housing sides, then moving to the gun assembly on the pitch bone: a breech block, parallel steel rails running along z, and a row of glowing cyan torus coils spaced along the rail centerline.

I'm tightening the torus dimensions so the coils fit within the rail clearance, adjusting the gun's y-axis offset so everything stays under the housing top. Then placing the breech block near the mantlet opening and sketching a muzzle brake box at the barrel's far end.

I'm spacing out heat fins between the rails so they don't overlap the coil cylinders, then adding a thin glowing cyan rod running between the rails as the energy core.

Now I'm sticking to palette colors with a few custom ones, importing the glow effect, and setting up a textured plane for the eye. I'm also planning mirrored cheek details, a shoulder ammo box on one side, and ammo drums on the other -- checking the drum cylinder placements along the z-axis so they sit close without overlapping too much.

Confirming the drum spacing works vertically, adding striped texture to the drums, and making sure the housing, drum centers, and ammo box all fit within the body's x-axis limits. I'm also sketching a belt feed path from the ammo box and considering a small hazard warning decal plane on the housing's side near the cheek.

I decide to place the hazard chevron label instead on the rear face of the housing, slightly slanted downward, sized small enough to fit under the existing geometry without clashing with the ammo box or drum placement. Now I'm ready to write the code for this piece.

I'm planning out the cab shell geometry, thinking through dimensions for the box and a wedge-shaped windshield profile extruded across the vehicle's width.

Working out the slanted windshield slab, computing its angle and outward-facing normal so the glass plane sits flush with the hull's slope.

Still adjusting layer offsets...

Now I'm adding the roof details — mirrors with camera pods, hatch, roof rack, light bars with glow, sensor dome, and antenna array — plus an interior with dashboard, seats, and glowing screens visible through the glass.

Setting up the hull using a panelled kit piece, then adding a wedge nose with a front face, hazard stripe trim along the roof, and yellow side strips. I'm planning quick SVG textures for glass streaks, a "77" decal, warning labels, and hazard chevrons, plus a helper function for placing boxes and extruded parts attached to the body bone with color and direction options.

Adding merged bolt geometry... Now I'm sketching the door outlines, handle, and hazard chevron stripe details, then adjusting the mirror pod and arm positioning against the body box width.

I'm sketching out the roof light bars, antenna rods, and a sensor dome with a hatch, figuring out placement coordinates for each part.

I'm planning the vehicle body geometry using a moderate number of parts, defining the box dimensions and wheel placements along the x, y, and z axes.

I'm sketching out a helper function for adding body parts tied to the bone system, then thinking through textures like a grille mesh with a skull motif, hazard chevrons, and glowing headlights rendered as textured planes facing forward. I'm also working out the hood's slope by rotating a box around the x-axis so the front edge dips down, positioning it near the windshield base before moving on to the front bumper geometry.

Now I'm adding a hazard-stripe texture plane to the bumper's front face and sketching a plow blade as an extruded trapezoid with zigzag teeth along the bottom edge, working out the x,y,z offsets so everything stays within the vehicle's bounding box.

Next I'm placing a winch cylinder with a cable and torus hook near the bumper, then laying out headlight clusters with housing boxes, glowing lens planes, cyan DRL strips, and small cylindrical fog lamps on the fenders, followed by arched fender flares.

Still working out the fender flare geometry...

Working out the arc placement and sizing...

Now I'm adding the fender boxes, then planning the spike cones along the bumper top, small tow-hook toruses, and an antenna rod extending up from the hood.

Still placing body panels...

Still working out positions...

Splitting the plow blade into two wing segments on either side of the hook, leaving the center open so the winch hook isn't obscured, with mirrored teeth outlines and adding white as a text color option.

For the headlight lens I'm using a flat glowing plane rather than a textured one. For the skull emblem I'm sketching a grille SVG with a dark background, magenta/cyan mesh lines, and a central skull motif, then starting a hazard stripe SVG with a yellow pattern.

Now I'm adding glow effects to headlights and underglow bars, setting up panelled hull paint, and working out hood rib geometry and rotation angles for the tilted engine hood panels.

Placing fog lamps into the bumper as small cylinders with lens glow, then adding upward-pointing cone spikes along the bumper top at spaced x positions, skipping forward-facing corner spikes for simplicity. Now I'm ready to write out the final code, importing the glow helper and skipping unnecessary randomness.

I need to figure out how Ctx is typed within this single function since it's defined by the module itself, so I'll just treat it as being in scope rather than redeclaring it.

Now I'm sketching the cargo bed's geometry: a main box roughly 3 units wide, spanning y 1.2-2.6 and z -4 to 0.9, with a rear ramp hinged at y 1.3 that I'll keep closed like a vertical rear door rather than folded down. I'm sizing the main bed box and planning to use a paneled hull material from the clockwork kit for the body.

Adding ribbed side walls, a top deck plate, hatch covers with yellow trim, crates and ammo cans, plus angled missile pods with cylindrical tubes and conical warheads mounted on the deck sides.

I'll write a podGeoms helper that builds transformed frame, tube, and warhead geometries so they can merge by color, then plan the tail lights and rear neon strip with a thin ramp detail near the back edge.

Let me recheck positions: I need to narrow the ramp width so taillights at x ±1.3 don't overlap it, and verify the ramp slab closes the gap at the bed's rear wall properly.

For the ramp details, I'm planning a hazard chevron texture plane facing outward at the rear, plus hinge cylinders along the bottom edge and hydraulic rod details, and a license plate plane with text.

Then I'm placing the chevron band near the top of the ramp, a plate offset lower, and a magenta warning strip spanning the width. For the spare tire, I'm mounting it on the left side wall of the bed as a disc shape sized to fit within the box limits, alongside the existing wheel positions.

Adding exhaust stack cylinders at the rear corners tucked against the bed wall, plus small slatted vent boxes on the deck, and now sketching a thin whip antenna rising from the rear corner within the height limit.

Adding tie-down rings as small torus shapes along the deck perimeter, and now planning a glowing SVG-textured status panel plane on the side wall.

For the side wall I'm spacing vertical rib boxes every 0.7 units in z from -3.5 to 0.7, with horizontal rails, and fitting the status panel into one of the gaps between ribs around z=-1.9.

Now I'm placing a status panel at z=-1.75, a warning label plane near z=-0.35, and adding a yellow trim strip along the top edge of the hull. For the deck, I'm adding a top plate around y=2.36 with panel detailing and planning hatch placements.

I'll add three hatch boxes with yellow frame borders and torus handles along the deck, and consider adding a hinged joint for one hatch so it can open, keeping the hinge simple by anchoring it at the back edge.

Now I'm working out the deck layout: the turret ring sits near the front, so pods go on either side further back, while crates stack in a two-high arrangement centered behind the turret, sized and positioned to stay within the available deck space.

I'll set the deck top at 2.25, with a raised front command block up to 2.6 with a sloped face, and stack crates (0.5x0.35x0.5) plus ammo cans (0.3x0.22x0.14) on the rear deck so the top levels out around 2.6-2.82. Body wall spans y 1.3..2.25, ribs at 0.8 height, and the front raised block runs x ±1.3 from y 2.25 to 2.6.

I'm working out an extruded wedge shape for the sloped rear of that command block using a profile outline in the z-y plane, then adding a small seat ring disc near the turret base at radius 0.72.

Checking the overlap between the flat block top and the ring radius, I realize the dimensions clash, so I'm adjusting the top to run flat from z=0.0 to 0.9 and extending the front wall outline accordingly.

For the paint setup, I'm defining the hull paint as a panelled texture using the hull color with panel size 0.5, rivet spacing of 0.06, and scaling the texel density for the roughly 40 square meters of painted surface area across the hull and bed.

I'm sketching out the SVG textures needed: a yellow/black diagonal hazard stripe pattern, chevron markings for the ramp, a "WH-2077" identification plate with a dark border, and a status panel with cyan indicator bars.

Still writing textures... I'm adding a warning triangle with "DANGER / EXPLOSIVES" text, a stenciled "AMMO 77" crate texture on olive paint that wraps all six box faces, and for the kanji glyph "危険" I'm considering drawing it as simple rectangular strokes instead of relying on font rendering since it may not display correctly.

Now I'm designing the missile pods as a 2x3 grid of tubes, with each pod's local frame holding a dark hull box, cylindrical tube cutouts with black cap discs at the front, and protruding warhead cones tipped in olive trim.

I'm adjusting the weapon pod geometry so the tilted box doesn't dip below the deck, tweaking frame height and tube radius in a 2x2 arrangement, and adding a small pedestal support underneath to anchor it properly.

Now I'm setting up helper functions to build and merge geometries by color group—frame, dark tubes, olive heads, red tips—using BufferGeometryUtils to combine them with consistent attributes for flat shading, then defining shorthand functions like `part` and `box` to attach these parts to the body bone.

I'm positioning taillight housings and glow elements on either side of the rear, carefully checking that the light placement doesn't overlap with the ramp geometry, and layering red brake lights with a small white reverse lamp for detail before moving on to the exhaust pipes.

I'm placing the exhaust stack pair at the rear corners, working out heights, heat shield cages, angled cone caps, and rust/steel coloring to avoid clipping with the wall or ribs.

Next I'm positioning the spare tire flat on the deck near center-rear, then arranging hatches, crates, and pods around it so nothing overlaps on the cramped deck layout.

Still placing vents and hood details, then checking antenna placement against the pod positions to avoid overlap—settling on an antenna base cylinder with an outward-tilted whip rod and a glowing red bulb tip, plus a shorter secondary antenna nearby.

Now I'm working out tie-down rings around the deck edges as flat tori, plus side-wall rings facing outward, grouping these into a single steel-colored merged geometry, and starting on cyan neon strip placement along the bottom edge of the side wall.

For the ramp I'm adding the main hinged slab with painted panels and yellow trim border boxes, a chevron decal plane near the rear, and license plate and glyph decal planes positioned along the ramp surface.

I need the rod bones to attach explicitly to the correct joint since inheritance won't find the right one automatically, so I'm specifying the rampHinge joint directly. For the hazard decal, I'm adding a textured plane just off the ramp's back surface, working out the facing direction and axis orientation so it reads correctly from behind.

For the orientation math, I'm reasoning through local axes: with forward pointing toward -Z, up along Y, the local x axis comes out as -X, which means the texture reads correctly to a viewer standing behind. I'm now working through the same logic for the side panels, figuring out which direction counts as "right" for a viewer positioned along +X looking toward -X.

Now I'm designing the cargo bed hatch joint -- placing the hinge at the rear edge with a hatch panel, yellow support frame, torus handle, and small indicator light, then assigning it the "hinge" role for the rigging system.

I'm also mapping out remaining body details: missile pod racks, the chassis frame layering under the bed, yellow trim strips along the deck edges, and armored corner posts with bolt heads at the four corners.

Now I'm thinking of modeling the main body as an extruded chamfered hexagonal cross-section running the vehicle's length, defining the outline points to shape a sloped armor profile along the top and sides.

Then I'm adding a deck plate as a thin box on top of the body, settling on a DECK height constant of 2.3 to anchor where props and ribs will sit, and starting to place thin side ribs along the hull faces.

Still adjusting rail and strip positions to avoid conflicts with the panels and chamfers...

Tallying up the part count across body, ribs, rails, trim, panels, pods, exhaust, vents, antennas, and ramp pieces, I land around 120 parts, which feels reasonable for triangle count. Time to write the actual code now.

Writing SVG hazard and chevron textures...

Still designing icon SVGs...

Now I'm thinking through the spare tyre geometry — a rubber cylinder for the tread, a steel hub cylinder, and tread blocks arranged in a ring around the perimeter using rotated box geometries merged together.

I'm also adding mounting details: steel straps over the hub and a small glowing cyan accent disc. Now I'm writing a helper function that composes transformation matrices to position, rotate, and scale cloned geometries before merging them into a single mesh.

Building pod assembly function...

Adding tip cones with neon red color, a rear exhaust plate, and a yellow cross-stripe band. I'm also working out the pedestal geometry under the body, checking the pod's lower corner clearance against the deck and adjusting the center height to avoid dipping below it.

I'm designing the vent stack with a base frame, slatted louvres, and a sloped cap, merging parts to minimize the object count across all four vents, then adding a steel exhaust pipe cylinder positioned above the deck.

For the exhaust, I'm adding clamp rings, a top rim trim piece, and considering a heat shield, but simplifying to a small shroud box behind the pipe rather than a complex curved cylinder, then merging the clamp geometry to keep it efficient before finalizing all the parts.

Now I'm setting up the paint palette using only the defined color constants, building panelled hull textures with rivets, adding mud grime near the base through a height-based color mix, and blending hull tones with a smoothstep gradient for the base paint layer.

Still extruding body sections...

Working out rib positions along z and placing status, warning, and glyph panels at their respective midpoint slots, with sizing for each panel type.

With the layout settled, I'm ready to write the final code, using a glow helper that wraps textured plane parts for the panel surfaces.

I'm noticing the deck height barely clears the hull, leaving many deck items like missile pods, crates, spare tyre, exhaust, and antennas exceeding the box top—so I'm considering whether to lower the deck or apply a scale-down transform to everything deck-related to fit within bounds.

Lowering the deck itself causes problems: wall details and hull wall thickness are hard-coded at specific heights, so shrinking the hull profile would make those inconsistent and float incorrectly. I think keeping the deck height fixed and instead shrinking the individual deck items (like pods) to stay within the 0.3m clearance above the deck is more tractable, even though it's a bit tedious.

So I'm scaling down the pods to half size via a scale matrix, adjusting their vertical position accordingly. For crates, cans, the spare tyre, exhaust, and antennas, I'm reducing heights and repositioning them -- laying the tire flatter, shortening the exhaust and antenna, and placing cans directly on the floor instead of stacking -- while leaving vents and the hatch mostly as-is since they're already short enough.

Adjusting remaining heights...
